note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Gallery index 0 shows a real in-ground leafy tuft, while indices 4–5 show the original narrow crowded green and dry heads. Bob Harms' exact-species index 10 adds an attached dense flowering head with a printed metric ruler. Seek a tufted perennial with a contracted 8–25 cm upright panicle, but neither the actual root fibers nor knotty rhizome is exposed in index 0. All indices here are ZERO-BASED.
tiles.status: TRUE LIVING GRASS BASE + TWO OPEN-FIELD FULL HEAD PHOTOS; EXPOSED CROWN STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE CROWN AND TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: Exact-source gallery index 0 shows the living basal tuft; indices 1–2 show leaf blade and exterior sheath attachments, NOT a measured true ligule. At the INNER blade–sheath junction look for the published 0.2–0.5 mm hair-fringe ligule with a physical 1-mm scale. Expose a connected rooted crown and knotty basal rhizome before labelling them; both remain hidden in existing photos.
tiles.status: REAL BASAL GROWTH/LEAF CONTEXT PRESENT; EXPOSED RHIZOME AND HAIR-FRINGED LIGULE STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE A RIPE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Gallery index 3 shows real overlapping pale multiflowered spikelets without a calibrated ruler; Harms index 10 shows attached flowering structures with a printed metric scale, index 11 shows crowded attached mature spikelets beside a ruler, and index 12 shows an actual source-labelled detached reproductive dissection. Published 4–10 mm spikelet size and 4–10 florets are NOT independently measured from the images here; count ripe florets and verify the scale before adding exact measurement arrows.
tiles.status: ATTACHED AND DETACHED REPRODUCTIVE PHOTOS AVAILABLE; INDIVIDUAL PARTS AND MEASUREMENTS STILL NEED VALIDATION

tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, LEMMA AND MUCRO
tiles.details: Two one-keeled, one-veined membranous glumes are published at approximately 3–4 mm and similar in length. The fertile lemma is about 3–4 mm, three-veined, toothed or shallowly split at the tip, with at most a short mucro rather than a long awn. Harms index 12 is an ACTUAL mature spikelet dissection and index 11 supplies attached-spikelet context; neither presently supports independently verified arrows to each glume vein, lemma nerve hair or tiny mucro. Calibrate the existing source dissection before requesting duplicate generic anatomy.
tiles.status: REAL DISSECTION PHOTO EXISTS — FINE GLUME/LEMMA VEINS, HAIRS AND MUCRO NOT CERTIFIED

tiles.heading: 05 · COMPARE LOCAL TRIDENS
tiles.details: Gallery indices 6–7 are PURPLETOP (Tridens flavus), with open or drooping panicles that can be purple or straw-colored. Indices 8–9 are TEXAS TRIDENS (T. texanus), with fine flexuous branches and separated spikelet groups. ALL FOUR are different-species comparisons, NOT white tridens. Indices 0–5 and 10–12 show white tridens. Color and bare branch bases alone are not species proof; inspect glumes and lemma nerve-hair distribution when head silhouettes overlap.
tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE GROSS PHOTOS AVAILABLE; MATCHED MATURE DISSECTIONS MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · PROVE BEFORE PUBLIC-FINISHED
tiles.details: Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS. Existing Harms indices 10–12 already provide attached reproductive views and a real detached dissection; do NOT request another generic dissection until these are reviewed for measurable glumes and lemma details. Still obtain a Central Texas source-verified rooted flowering plant, exposed rhizome/crown and a true 0.2–0.5 mm inner ligule with 1-mm scale. For reproductive certainty, independently validate the glume veins, three-veined lemma, basal hair distribution and mucro on Harms index 12 at sufficient resolution, or obtain a sharper calibrated macro if impossible. NEEDS_SITE_QA: check all 13 panels, 18 existing markers, source-specific Bob Harms credited educational permission, other photo licenses, different-species labels and mobile rendering.
tiles.short: Same-plant collar, glumes and lemma required

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: WHITE TRIDENS: find a narrow, straight, DENSE panicle with spikelets pressed to the axis. The green and pale mature photographs show this architecture. Mature glumes are nearly equal and about 4 mm; lemma faces largely hairless or hairy just at the base. Confirm glume/lemma measurements on an intact ripe spikelet, not whiteness.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: See the first SOURCE-LABELLED PHOTO: use gross branches and spikelets as starting clues, not independent expert taxon confirmation.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Exact-source gallery index 0 shows the living basal tuft; indices 1–2 show leaf blade and exterior sheath attachments, NOT a measured true ligule. At the INNER blade–sheath junction look for the published 0.2–0.5 mm hair-fringe ligule with a physical 1-mm scale. Expose a connected rooted crown and knotty basal rhizome before labelling them; both remain hidden in existing photos.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Gallery index 3 shows real overlapping pale multiflowered spikelets without a calibrated ruler; Harms index 10 shows attached flowering structures with a printed metric scale, index 11 shows crowded attached mature spikelets beside a ruler, and index 12 shows an actual source-labelled detached reproductive dissection. Published 4–10 mm spikelet size and 4–10 florets are NOT independently measured from the images here; count ripe florets and verify the scale before adding exact measurement arrows.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Against T. flavus, look for narrowly appressed rather than broad drooping panicle branches; color varies for both. Against T. texanus, the packed almost continuous head versus an often flexuous sparse head is helpful, but dissect a mature spikelet: almost glabrous lemmas (except sometimes extreme base) and nearly equal glumes.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: WHITE TRIDENS: find a narrow, straight, DENSE panicle with spikelets pressed to the axis. The green and pale mature photographs show this architecture. Mature glumes are nearly equal and about 4 mm; lemma faces largely hairless or hairy just at the base. Confirm glume/lemma measurements on an intact ripe spikelet, not whiteness.
memory_rule: ALBESCENS narrow packed; FLAVUS wide drooping; TEXANUS flexuous separated. Confirm at mature GLUMES and 3-NERVED LEMMA.
safety_note: Now four more individually licensed source species photos in addition to two original heads, plus four old DIFFERENT-species panels. Root rhizome and true ciliate hair ligule NOT exposed in any new view; micro characters still published source traits not certified on pixels; keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.
field_rule: Species-level Tridens confidence requires panicle architecture PLUS mature spikelet/glume/lemma anatomy; do not identify from pigmentation alone.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: Against T. flavus, look for narrowly appressed rather than broad drooping panicle branches; color varies for both. Against T. texanus, the packed almost continuous head versus an often flexuous sparse head is helpful, but dissect a mature spikelet: almost glabrous lemmas (except sometimes extreme base) and nearly equal glumes.
